episodes.candidate_episode_scope: Only the exact House choices listed for: Whether to bar firearm-retailer-specific merchant category code requirements and create a complaint, cure, and injunction process.

chronological_action_sequence.implemented_exact_action_meaning: The House choice was whether to pass H.R. 1181, barring payment-card networks and covered processors from requiring or assigning merchant category codes that specifically identify firearms retailers. The Attorney General would investigate complaints and could seek an injunction after notice and a cure period, while the bill would preempt related State and local code rules subject to specified transaction-integrity exceptions.

limitations: The bill creates no private right of action.
The preemption rule preserves compliance with laws on disputes, fraud, illegal or suspicious activity, data breaches, and cyber risks.
The Attorney General must establish the complaint process within 90 days after enactment.
A violating network or entity has 30 days to cure after notice before the Attorney General may seek an injunction.
This candidate does not establish motive, ideology, a broad issue position, or a synthesis conclusion.
episodes.material_policy_differences: The measure regulates merchant coding rather than firearm possession, purchase eligibility, or facility carry.
episodes.neutral_policy_question: Whether to bar firearm-retailer-specific merchant category code requirements and create a complaint, cure, and injunction process.
